domains.name: Screening
domains.description: Screening: determining a client's appropriateness/eligibility for admission (Core Function 1).

domains.name: Intake
domains.description: Intake: administrative and assessment procedures for admission (Core Function 2).

domains.name: Orientation
domains.description: Orientation: informing the client of rules, services, goals, costs, and rights (Core Function 3).

domains.name: Assessment
domains.description: Assessment: evaluating strengths, needs, and problems to inform treatment (Core Function 4).

domains.name: Treatment Planning
domains.description: Treatment Planning: collaboratively setting problems, goals, methods, and timetables (Core Function 5).

domains.name: Counseling
domains.description: Counseling: applying individual, group, and family methods toward treatment goals (Core Function 6).

domains.name: Case Management
domains.description: Case Management: coordinating services on the client's behalf (Core Function 7).

domains.name: Crisis Intervention
domains.description: Crisis Intervention: responding to acute emotional/physical distress and ensuring safety (Core Function 8).

domains.name: Client Education
domains.description: Client Education: information on addiction, services, and prevention/recovery (Core Function 9).

domains.name: Referral
domains.description: Referral: connecting clients to resources for needs the program cannot meet (Core Function 10).

domains.name: Reports and Recordkeeping
domains.description: Reports and Recordkeeping: charting, documentation, and required reports (Core Function 11).

domains.name: Consultation
domains.description: Consultation: collaborating with other professionals for comprehensive, quality care (Core Function 12).

competencies.statement: The learner can screen a client to determine appropriateness and eligibility for admission to a program.
competencies.description: Applies screening criteria/tools to an admission decision.

competencies.statement: The learner can carry out the administrative and assessment procedures for program admission (intake).
competencies.description: Completes intake steps and required paperwork correctly.

competencies.statement: The learner can orient a client to program rules, services, goals, costs, and client rights.
competencies.description: Conveys orientation information clearly and completely.

competencies.statement: The learner can assess a client's strengths, needs, and problems to inform a treatment plan.
competencies.description: Gathers and organizes assessment information appropriately.

competencies.statement: The learner can develop a treatment plan with the client, identifying problems, setting goals, and agreeing on steps, methods, and timetables.
competencies.description: Builds a collaborative, measurable treatment plan.

competencies.statement: The learner can apply appropriate individual, group, and family counseling methods to help a client work toward treatment goals.
competencies.description: Selects/uses a suitable, evidence-based counseling approach.

competencies.statement: The learner can coordinate services and activities on a client's behalf (case management).
The learner can respond appropriately to a client in acute emotional or physical distress (crisis intervention).
competencies.description: Prioritizes safety and takes appropriate escalation steps.

competencies.statement: The learner can educate clients about addiction, available services, and prevention/recovery.
The learner can refer clients to community resources that meet needs the program cannot.
competencies.description: Makes appropriate, well-matched referrals with follow-through.

competencies.statement: The learner can chart, document, and prepare required reports accurately (recordkeeping).
competencies.description: Documents completely, objectively, and within confidentiality rules.

competencies.statement: The learner can consult and collaborate with other professionals to ensure comprehensive, quality care.
